releases.name: ai-hedge-fund 2.7.1
releases.body:
### Changes

- **Reopen a saved backtest.** On the mandate picker, each mandate's past runs sit on the right, newest first, up to 12. Right arrow or tab moves into that list. Enter opens the saved result in the same view a live backtest ends on: the curve, the stats, and the tape, with nothing fetched. Left arrow returns to the mandates. A file that will not parse fails in the UI.

releases.name: ai-hedge-fund 2.7.0
releases.body:
### Changes

- **Pay per call with x402.** Set `X402_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY` to a Base wallet holding USDC and each Financial Datasets request pays for itself. Install the extra with `pip install 'aihf[x402]'`. The app asks for an API key or a wallet key the first time it needs data. When both are set, the API key is what gets billed. x402 serves the last 365 days, non-professional use.

- **The scorecard moves the weights.** An `allocation` block multiplies each pod's capital slice and each analyst's blend weight by `clip(1 + slope × t-stat, floor, cap)`. Nothing moves until 20 graded dates or periods. A cut analyst keeps a quarter of its weight, and the cap is 2×. A minute fund rescores once a day. A mandate with no `allocation` block keeps the weights as written. New funds from the app include it.

- **Drawdown halving, plus caps on beta, sector, and vol.** At `halve_drawdown_pct` the book runs at half size until NAV recovers. New funds from the app halve at 10%, under the 20% stop-out. `max_beta`, `max_sector_pct`, and `max_volatility` stay off until you set them. Beta is an OLS fit on about 100 daily returns, shrunk toward 1. A sector over its cap scales the whole book. Volatility

releases.name: ai-hedge-fund 2.6.4
releases.body:
### Changes

- **Square-root market impact.** Every fill pays impact on top of the half-spread and the commission: Y × daily volatility × sqrt(order / 20-day average volume). Y defaults to 1.0. Volatility is the sample sigma of daily log returns over those same bars. A name with no history, or fewer than three bars, pays no impact. A minute fund's order is measured against a whole day's volume. The orders table splits the cost into spread, impact, and commission, and shows the order as a percent of ADV.

- **No-trade band.** An add smaller than `min_trade_pct` of equity waits and is retried next cycle. The default is 0.5%. A trim, a close, or a flip always goes through.

Both are defaults, so an existing mandate picks them up on upgrade. Set `impact_coefficient: 0` and `min_trade_pct: 0` to get the previous behavior back.

releases.name: ai-hedge-fund 2.6.3
releases.body:
### Changes

- **Net cap.** `max_net_exposure` clamps |longs minus shorts|. The heavier side is scaled down until the book sits on the band, and the weight that comes off stays in cash. Leave it unset and there is no net band, which is how every existing mandate behaves.

- **Drawdown stop-out.** `max_drawdown_pct` measures NAV against its peak. A ledger written before the peak was tracked measures from starting capital. At the line the fund sells everything at the next close and stays in cash. The analysts are not asked again until you raise the limit. New funds from the app default to 20%. An existing mandate is unchanged until you set it.

- **Volume cap.** `max_adv_pct` limits an order to that share of the name's 20-day average daily volume. A name with no volume history is left uncapped.

releases.name: ai-hedge-fund 2.6.2
releases.body:
### Changes

- **Each view is graded at its own horizon.** Every analyst declares how long a call should take to play out, and the engine stamps that on the view. The scorecard judges the view there, instead of at the fund's next rebalance. Buffett, Munger, Graham, and Lynch are graded at one year (252 trading days), Druckenmiller at 126 days, and post-earnings drift at 60 days. A view the ledger has not reached yet shows as pending. Ledgers written before this still grade, using the horizon the model declares today. The fund builder shows the horizon next to each analyst. Position sizing is unchanged.

readmeExcerpt: # AI Hedge Fund This is a proof of concept for an AI-powered hedge fund. The goal of this project is to explore the use of AI to make trading decisions. This project is for **educational** purposes only and is not intended for real trading or investment. Note: the system does not actually make any trades. ## Disclaimer This project is for **educational and research purposes only**. - Not intended for real trading or investment - No investment advice or guarantees provided - Creator assumes no liability for financial losses - Consult a financial advisor for investment decisions - Past performance does not indicate future results By using this software, you agree to use it solely for learning purposes. ## How to Install ```bash pipx install aihf ``` (or `uv tool install aihf`, or `pip install aihf` into an environment of your choice) Then run it from anywhere: ```bash aihf ``` ### API keys The app asks for keys the first time it needs them and saves them to `~/.hedge-fund/.env` — nothing to configure up front. It needs: - A [Financial Datasets](https://financialdatasets.ai) API key, for prices, fundamentals, and earnings. Or, instead of a key, the private key of a Base wallet holding USDC: every call then pays for itself with [x402](https://docs.financialdatasets.ai/x402) (`pip install 'aihf[x402]'`; last 365 days of data, non-professional use). - One model API key for the investor agents. Supported providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, xAI, Kimi, TypeSafe (Jev). Keys exported in your shell always win over the saved file. ## How to Run ### Interactive app ```bash aihf ``` With no arguments, this launches the interactive terminal app. It has two modes: - **Paper trading** — your funds, each with a ledger of real market days and fake money. Highlight a fund to see what its next run will do; press enter to run it through the next completed session (an approval step shows the exact decision about to execute before anything trades), `s` for its full session history, `h`/`r` for the kill switch. Build a new fund from the same list: strategies, capital, cadence, tickers, and it is live. Every session is appended to a hash-chained ledger in `~/.hedge-fund/paper//`, so NAV is a track record, not a reset. - **Backtesting** — replay a fund over history and watch its equity curve draw against its benchmark. Results are saved to `~/.hedge-fund/research/`. Fund definitions live in `~/.hedge-fund/mandates/` and carry no tickers; you pick the universe per backtest. ## Development ```bash git clone https://github.com/virattt/ai-hedge-fund.git cd ai-hedge-fund poetry install poetry run aihf poetry run pytest hedge_fund ``` ## How to Contribute 1. Fork the repository 2. Create a feature branch 3. Commit your changes 4. Push to the branch 5. Create a Pull Request **Important**: Please keep your pull requests small and focused. This will make it easier to review and merge. ## Feature Requests If you have a feature request, please open an [issue](https://github.com/virattt/ai-hedge-fund/issues) and make sure it is tagged with `enhancement`. ## License This project is licensed under the MIT License - see the LICENSE file for details.
readmeHtml:
AI Hedge Fund

This is a proof of concept for an AI-powered hedge fund. The goal of this project is to explore the use of AI to make trading decisions. This project is for educational purposes only and is not intended for real trading or investment.

Note: the system does not actually make any trades.

Disclaimer

This project is for educational and research purposes only.

  • Not intended for real trading or investment
  • No investment advice or guarantees provided
  • Creator assumes no liability for financial losses
  • Consult a financial advisor for investment decisions
  • Past performance does not indicate future results

By using this software, you agree to use it solely for learning purposes.

How to Install

pipx install aihf

(or uv tool install aihf, or pip install aihf into an environment of your choice)

Then run it from anywhere:

aihf

API keys

The app asks for keys the first time it needs them and saves them to ~/.hedge-fund/.env — nothing to configure up front. It needs:

  • A Financial Datasets API key, for prices, fundamentals, and earnings. Or, instead of a key, the private key of a Base wallet holding USDC: every call then pays for itself with x402 (pip install 'aihf[x402]'; last 365 days of data, non-professional use).
  • One model API key for the investor agents. Supported providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, xAI, Kimi, TypeSafe (Jev).

Keys exported in your shell always win over the saved file.

How to Run

Interactive app

aihf

With no arguments, this launches the interactive terminal app. It has two modes:

  • Paper trading — your funds, each with a ledger of real market days and fake money. Highlight a fund to see what its next run will do; press enter to run it through the next completed session (an approval step shows the exact decision about to execute before anything trades), s for its full session history, h/r for the kill switch. Build a new fund from the same list: strategies, capital, cadence, tickers, and it is live. Every session is appended to a hash-chained ledger in ~/.hedge-fund/paper/<name>/, so NAV is a track record, not a reset.
  • Backtesting — replay a fund over history and watch its equity curve draw against its benchmark. Results are saved to ~/.hedge-fund/research/. Fund definitions live in ~/.hedge-fund/mandates/ and carry no tickers; you pick the universe per backtest.

Development

git clone https://github.com/virattt/ai-hedge-fund.git
cd ai-hedge-fund
poetry install
poetry run aihf
poetry run pytest hedge_fund

How to Contribute

  1. Fork the repository
  2. Create a feature branch
  3. Commit your changes
  4. Push to the branch
  5. Create a Pull Request

Important: Please keep your pull requests small and focused. This will make it easier to review and merge.

Feature Requests

If you have a feature request, please open an issue and make sure it is tagged with enhancement.

License

This project is licensed under the MIT License - see the LICENSE file for details.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An experimental framework for simulating algorithmic trading strategies using multi-agent LLM consensus.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This project explores the intersection of quantitative finance and generative AI by simulating a hedge fund managed entirely by large language models. It deploys multiple distinct AI agents—each adopting a specific persona like fundamental analyst, technical trader, or risk manager. These agents analyze real-time market data, financial news, and historical trends to debate and propose trading actions. The system aggregates their insights using a sophisticated consensus mechanism to finalize portfolio allocations. It provides a robust backtesting engine to evaluate the performance of these AI-driven strategies against historical market conditions.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent architecture: Employs diverse AI personas to provide varied perspectives on market conditions.
Live data ingestion: Connects to financial APIs to pull real-time stock prices and relevant news articles.
Consensus mechanism: Utilizes a voting algorithm to determine the final trade action based on agent debates.
Backtesting engine: Allows users to simulate strategies on historical data to evaluate potential returns.
Risk management constraints: Enforces strict hardcoded limits to prevent catastrophic AI hallucinations during trading.
